items.title: Carney frames C$1.6B AI investment as national security imperative
items.excerpt: Canada's government is putting C$1.6 billion into Cohere's Series E, which Prime Minister Mark Carney framed as a sovereign-AI and national-security investment ahead of the Canada-EU summit, where von der Leyen pledged joint work on AI safety rules and standards.

history_match.title: Investment summit: German government strikes AI deal with Nvidia

items.title: Canada to join EU network of supercomputers
items.excerpt: Canada will join the EU's network of supercomputers. POLITICO calls the compute-sharing deal a first step toward middle-power cooperation on AI, announced around the Canada-EU summit.

history_match.title: EXCLUSIVE: China offered European Commission to join its AI alliance

items.title: Frontier AI one of greatest threats to Canadians as Ottawa releases national security strategy
items.excerpt: Canada released its first national security strategy in more than two decades, 'The Plan for a Stronger Canada'. Officials named frontier AI models among the greatest current threats, and the plan promises more intelligence and cyber-defence capability.

items.title: Austria pitches for United Nations AI security centre in Vienna
items.excerpt: At a 31-country virtual meeting on frontier-AI control co-hosted by Norway and Finland, Austria proposed a UN AI centre in Vienna and Singapore floated an incident-reporting pilot. An expert-level process will continue, apparently without the US or China taking part.

items.title: Sánchez's wife sues Spanish opposition over AI deepfake
items.excerpt: Begoña Gómez filed a legal complaint for 'identity theft' against Spain's People's Party over an AI-generated video of her used in a PP campaign ad. The case lands ahead of a November election and touches on EU tech rules. (New filing in a story already published on 10-26.)

history_match.title: Opposition deepfake video of Spanish PM's wife sparks outrage before election

items.title: A Defense Contractor Gave Their Personal AI Agent Access to a Secure Pentagon System
items.excerpt: Sources tell WIRED that an Accenture employee's personal Claude agent ran on a DOD network for two months before it was found and the vulnerability patched. The case raises questions about agent-access policy in government systems.

items.title: UK Home Office May Face Investigation Over Use of OpenAI Tech
items.excerpt: A UK government watchdog is weighing a probe into the Home Office's use of ChatGPT-based tools to process asylum claims, over concerns about the tools' accuracy and the secrecy around their use.

history_match.title: Home Office asylum AI flunks one in five accuracy checks

items.title: UK Politician Jess Asato Got Deepfaked. Now She's Taking xAI to Court
items.excerpt: Labour MP Jess Asato, herself a target of Grok-generated sexual deepfakes, is taking legal action against xAI, arguing it unlawfully used her image without consent. The case could set a precedent on AI-company liability. (Interview format.)

items.title: Trump's AI use to inform military operations questioned by House duo
items.excerpt: The ranking members of two House committees asked for a closed-door briefing on the administration's use of AI to inform military operations. The request covers document-retention policy, vendor contracts and cybersecurity safeguards.

items.title: DoD issues guidance for procuring 'unbiased' AI systems
items.excerpt: The Pentagon issued non-binding acquisition guidance, with templates and sample contract language, for buying AI that meets the administration's 'truth-seeking' and 'ideological neutrality' principles under EO 14319 and OMB memo M-26-04.

items.title: Attorney General James Uthmeier ... Files Lawsuit Against A2E for Enabling AI-Generated CSAM
items.excerpt: Florida's attorney general filed a civil suit against Rengstorff Consulting, operator of the A2E AI platform and apps. The suit alleges the tools let users generate child sexual abuse material and non-consensual sexualized images of Floridians. (Release date Oct 28, 2026; time-of-day not given.)

items.title: FTC expands personalized pricing scrutiny as states, Congress, regulators turn up pressure
items.excerpt: The FTC sent Section 6(b) orders to nine companies, including Delta, United, Uber, DoorDash, Instacart, Target and Walmart, demanding details on how personal data and AI are used to set consumer prices and gig-worker pay.

history_match.title: FTC demands Anthropic execs testify in expanding AI safety probe

items.title: Google AI gets cagey when asked who won the 2020 elections
items.excerpt: Days before the US midterms, Google's AI answers dodge the question of who won the 2020 US election, though they are more forthright when asked from outside the US.

history_match.title: LLMs Are Still Making Election Deepfakes Just Days Before the US Midterms

items.title: Trump ignored intel on China's Nvidia spy to protect company's stock, report says
items.excerpt: A report says US officials investigated a suspected Chinese intelligence asset with access close to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, and that the White House did not act on the intel. Attributed to the report; Huang called the ties 'normal'.

items.title: Voters in Texas agree: They hate data centers
items.excerpt: AI data-center siting has become a midterm issue in rural Texas, where energy and water concerns have turned voters against Republican support for data-center buildouts.

history_match.title: Data centers face a sweeping new power regime

items.title: EU privacy advocates accuse US data annotation firm of snooping on contractors
items.excerpt: noyb filed five GDPR complaints in four EU member states over alleged tracking of AI data-annotation workers on Scale AI's Outlier platform.

items.title: Washington's Overlooked Leverage Over China's Chip Ambitions
items.excerpt: Analysis: China's new immersion lithography tools are not yet production-ready, but continued servicing by the US and its allies speeds their progress. The author argues existing US export-control rules already allow a response. (Commentary.)

items.title: Back in the Chat: California and New York Take Diverging Paths in Second Wave of Chatbot Regulations
items.excerpt: FPF compares New York's newly signed S 9051B, which restricts AI companion-chatbot features for minors, with California's approach in the second wave of state chatbot laws. (Analysis; the NY signing was already published 10-29.)

history_match.title: New York Gov. Hochul signs law barring AI companion chatbots from simulating human relationships with minors

items.title: Who Wins, Who Sues, Who Pays the Price
items.excerpt: The Tow Center's updated tracker of AI licensing deals and lawsuits between publishers and AI companies shows striking geographic inequities in who gets paid and who sues.
